blocks.content:
A candidate must:
• Be a citizen of India
• Be at least 35 years old
• Be qualified to become a member of the Lok Sabha
• Not hold any office of profit
The oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 58 details qualifications: must be an Indian citizen, at least 35 years old, qualified for Lok Sabha membership, and free from any office of profit.
Article 56 specifies a 5-year term of office with eligibility for re-election.
An outgoing President continues in office beyond the 5-year period until their successor officially assumes office.
The Oath of Office is administered by the Chief Justice of India, or by the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court in the CJI's absence.

blocks.content:
• Term: 5 years
• Eligible for re-election
• Continues until successor assumes office

items: A presidential candidate must be qualified for membership of the Lok Sabha (not Rajya Sabha).
The minimum age requirement for the President of India is 35 years.
In the absence of the Chief Justice of India, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court administers the oath.
